title: The School of Athens
description: Raphael brings philosophy and mathematics into a single architectural space. At the lower right, a group gathers around a geometric construction. The fresco’s perspective gives the scene its measured depth.
license: Public domain. Faithful reproduction via Wikimedia Commons; source imagery credited to the Vatican.

title: The Elements of Euclid
artist: Oliver Byrne · Reproduction by Dr Mirko Junge
description: Byrne’s edition uses red, blue and yellow shapes to carry a geometric argument. This plate presents the Pythagorean theorem, linking the squares on the sides of a right triangle.
license: Public domain. The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid, 1847. Reproduction via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Melencolia I
artist: Albrecht Dürer · The Metropolitan Museum of Art
description: A polyhedron, sphere, compass and magic square surround the seated figure in Dürer’s engraving. Instruments of measurement share the scene with the unresolved work of thought.
license: Public domain artwork; museum image released under CC0. Fletcher Fund, 1919. Accession 19.73.85.

title: Nova methodus · Tabula XII
artist: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz · BEIC digital library
description: Curves, tangent lines and geometric constructions accompany Leibniz’s 1684 paper on differential calculus. The plate records a formative moment in the study of continuous change.
license: Public domain. PD-old-100-expired; digitized by the Biblioteca Europea di Informazione e Cultura (BEIC), via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Mysterium Cosmographicum
artist: Johannes Kepler · Engraving by Christophorus Leibfried
description: Kepler’s historical model nests the Platonic solids between planetary spheres. The engraving illustrates his early attempt to explain the spacing of the planets through geometry.
license: Public domain. PD-old-100-expired; reproduction via Wikimedia Commons.
